questions.q:
The Union Cabinet approved India's NDC 3.0 on 25 March 2026. Consider the following statements:
1. It covers the period 1 January 2031 to 31 December 2035.
2. It targets a 47 per cent cut in the emissions intensity of GDP from 2005 levels.
3. It targets a 60 per cent non-fossil share of cumulative installed electricity capacity.
4. It targets an additional carbon sink of 2.5 to 3 billion tonnes of CO2 equivalent by 2035.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The carbon-sink target for 2035 is 3.5 to 4.0 billion tonnes of CO2 equivalent; 2.5 to 3 billion was the 2030 target. India had already reached 52.57 per cent non-fossil capacity by February 2026, meeting its 50 per cent goal for 2030 five years early.

questions.q:
The 15th Conference of the Parties to the Convention on Migratory Species (CMS COP15) was held at Campo Grande, Brazil, from 23 to 29 March 2026. Consider the following statements:
1. It added 40 species, subspecies and populations to the CMS Appendices, 20 of them to Appendix I.
2. It advanced the Samarkand Strategic Plan for Migratory Species 2024-2032.
3. Appendix II of CMS lists migratory species that are in danger of extinction.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Appendix I of CMS covers migratory species threatened with extinction, which Parties must strictly protect; Appendix II lists species with an unfavourable conservation status that need international cooperation. The Hudsonian godwit, down 95 per cent in four decades, was among the species discussed.

questions.q: A UN interim update to the State of the World's Migratory Species report was released in 2026. Which of the following species moved from 'Extinct in the Wild' to 'Endangered' in it?
questions.e: The Scimitar-horned Oryx recovered from Extinct in the Wild to Endangered, while the Saiga Antelope improved from Endangered to Near Threatened. The update found 49 per cent of CMS-listed populations declining (44 per cent two years earlier) and 24 per cent at risk of extinction.
questions.h: Oryx back from the wild-extinct list.

questions.q:
India submitted its 7th National Report to the Convention on Biological Diversity. Consider the following statements:
1. It is submitted under Article 26 of the CBD.
2. It tracks 23 national biodiversity targets under the updated NBSAP (2024-30).
3. Forest and tree cover was 25.17 per cent of land area, and 24.1 million hectares were restored against a Bonn Challenge pledge of 26 million.
4. India has already exceeded its Bonn Challenge pledge.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Restoration of 24.1 million hectares leaves India nearing, not exceeding, its pledge of 26 million hectares by 2030. Land degradation still affects 29.77 per cent of the country. The report was prepared by MoEFCC with inputs from 33 ministries and UNDP support.

questions.q:
The MoEFCC submitted India's First National Report on implementation of the Nagoya Protocol on Access and Benefit Sharing. Consider the following statements:
1. The Nagoya Protocol is a supplementary agreement under the Convention on Biological Diversity concerned with fair sharing of benefits from genetic resources.
2. It was adopted at the 1992 Rio Earth Summit.
3. India implements it through the Biological Diversity Act, 2002 with the National Biodiversity Authority, State Biodiversity Boards and Biodiversity Management Committees.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Nagoya Protocol was adopted in 2010 and came into force in 2014; it is the CBD itself that was adopted at Rio in 1992. Access requires prior informed consent and benefit sharing follows mutually agreed terms.

questions.q:
The WMO released its 'State of the Global Climate 2025' report on World Meteorological Day (23 March 2026). Consider the following statements:
1. It included Earth's energy imbalance (EEI) as a key climate indicator for the first time.
2. 2025 was the second or third warmest year on record, about 1.43 degrees Celsius above the 1850-1900 average.
3. Ocean heat content reached a new record high in 2025.
4. Ocean heat content fell to a ten-year low in 2025.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: EEI measures the gap between energy absorbed from the Sun and energy radiated back to space; a positive value means the planet is heating. Ocean heat content rose to a record, so statement 4 is wrong, and 2015-2025 are the hottest 11 years on record.
questions.h: EEI added; ocean heat at record.

questions.q:
The MoEFCC designated the Bhavasagara Referral Centre of CMLRE, Kochi as the National Repository for Deep-Sea Fauna. Consider the following statements:
1. The designation is under Section 39 of the Biological Diversity Act, 2002.
2. CMLRE functions under the Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying.
3. The centre holds over 3,500 identified, geo-referenced voucher specimens.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: CMLRE (Centre for Marine Living Resources and Ecology) works under the Ministry of Earth Sciences. The centre is also custodian of type specimens of new deep-sea species from Indian waters.

questions.q: The Supreme Court took suo motu cognisance of reports that illegal sand mining threatens the National Chambal Sanctuary. Which one of the following describes the sanctuary correctly?
o: It lies at the tri-junction of Gujarat, Rajasthan and Madhya Pradesh and protects the Asiatic lion
It lies at the tri-junction of Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh and Rajasthan and holds the largest wild gharial population
It lies in Odisha and protects mainly the saltwater crocodile
It lies at the tri-junction of Uttarakhand, Uttar Pradesh and Bihar and protects the tiger
questions.e: The sanctuary protects the critically endangered gharial and red-crowned roof turtle and the endangered Ganges river dolphin. Sand mining destroys the sandbanks used for nesting.

questions.q:
Project Great Indian Bustard entered the fourth year of captive breeding in 2026. Consider the following statements:
1. The Great Indian Bustard is listed as Endangered on the IUCN Red List.
2. It is in Schedule I of the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972.
3. The Conservation Breeding Centre was set up in 2019 at Desert National Park, Jaisalmer.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Great Indian Bustard is Critically Endangered, not just Endangered. Two new chicks hatched in Rajasthan took the captive population to 70, and a chick also hatched in Kutch using an inter-State egg transfer.

questions.q:
India has 98 Ramsar sites as of 2026, up from 26 in 2014. Consider the following statements:
1. India ranks first in Asia and third in the world by number of Ramsar sites.
2. The 7th National Report to the CBD cites the growth of the Ramsar network as a sign of progress.
3. The Ramsar Convention was adopted in 1992 at the Rio Earth Summit.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Ramsar Convention on wetlands was adopted in 1971 at Ramsar, Iran, not in 1992 at Rio, so statement 3 is wrong. The 7th National Report highlights the rapid expansion of the Ramsar network, with India first in Asia and third globally.

questions.q:
Nearly 20,000 Olive Ridley turtle eggs were conserved in situ on Hope Island in Kakinada Bay, Andhra Pradesh. Consider the following statements:
1. Hope Island lies in Kakinada Bay near the Coringa Wildlife Sanctuary.
2. The Olive Ridley turtle is listed as Critically Endangered on the IUCN Red List.
3. The eggs were protected by the Wildlife Management Authority and Coringa Wildlife Sanctuary as in-situ conservation.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Olive Ridley is classified Vulnerable by the IUCN, though protected under Schedule I of the Wildlife (Protection) Act. In-situ conservation means protecting eggs where they are laid, rather than moving them to hatcheries.

questions.q:
The National Board for Wildlife approved Assam's proposal to rationalise the boundary of Pobitora Wildlife Sanctuary. Consider the following statements:
1. Pobitora Wildlife Sanctuary is located in West Bengal.
2. The National Board for Wildlife is a statutory body under the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972.
3. It is chaired by the Union Minister of Environment.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Pobitora is in Assam, noted for a high density of one-horned rhinoceros. The NBWL is statutory and is chaired by the Prime Minister, who is its head, with the Environment Minister as vice-chairperson.

questions.q:
MoEFCC published a draft amendment to the EIA Notification, 2006 to reduce delays at the State level. Consider the following statements:
1. The draft is issued under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986.
2. A Standing Authority on EIA in each State would take over the functions of the SEIAA for a maximum of five years if it is non-functional.
3. If a State Expert Appraisal Committee does not finish appraisal within 120 days, the proposal moves automatically to a Standing Committee via the Parivesh portal.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The standing bodies would act for a maximum of one year, not five. Delayed reconstitution of the three-year-tenure State bodies had held up environmental clearances.

questions.q: NHAI released the first National Highways Green Cover Index (NH-GCI) prepared with ISRO's National Remote Sensing Centre. Which one of the following is correct?
o: It covers all 1.5 lakh km of roads of the country including State highways
It was prepared by the Forest Survey of India with the Survey of India
It is a ranking of States by the number of trees planted
It measures vegetation cover along about 30,000 km of national highways in 24 States, in one-kilometre segments
questions.e: The Index implements the Green Highways Policy, 2015 and is published on the Bhuvan portal. It uses satellite-derived data to track green cover year on year.

questions.q:
The National Productivity Council (NPC) signed an agreement with the MoEFCC to act as the Environment Audit Designated Agency under the Environment Audit Rules, 2025. Consider the following statements:
1. NPC will manage the environmental audit framework, including eligibility criteria and registration of auditors.
2. NPC functions under the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change.
3. NPC is a constituent of the Tokyo-based Asian Productivity Organisation, of which India is a founding member.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: NPC is an autonomous body under the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade, Ministry of Commerce and Industry, not under MoEFCC, so statement 2 is wrong. It was set up in 1958 and belongs to the Asian Productivity Organisation.

questions.q:
The MoEFCC issued draft End-of-Life Vehicles (Amendment) Rules, 2026 on 27 March 2026. Consider the following statements:
1. The draft requires at least 10 per cent recycled steel in vehicles from 2026-27.
2. Insurance companies must register on State Pollution Control Board portals and ensure vehicle deposits.
3. Comments were invited until 26 June 2026.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Comments were due by 26 May 2026. IRDAI is to prescribe the responsibilities of insurers under the draft.
questions.h: 10 per cent recycled steel; comments to 26 May.

questions.q:
The MNRE notified emission standards under the National Green Hydrogen Mission. Match the products in List-I with the maximum emission limits in List-II:
List-I: A. Green hydrogen; B. Green ammonia; C. Green methanol
List-II: 1. 0.38 kg CO2e per kg; 2. 0.44 kg CO2e per kg; 3. 2 kg CO2e per kg
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: Green hydrogen is capped at 2 kg CO2e per kg of hydrogen, green ammonia at 0.38 and green methanol at 0.44 per kg. The Mission, approved in 2023, targets 125 GW of associated renewable capacity by 2030.

questions.q:
The International Solar Alliance (ISA) marked its Foundation Day on 11 March 2026. Consider the following statements:
1. India's Prime Minister envisioned the ISA as an 'alternative OPEC' for equitable energy.
2. It aggregates demand to cut the cost of solar finance and technology for LDCs and SIDS.
3. It was launched at COP26 in Glasgow.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The ISA was launched by India and France at COP21 in Paris (2015), not at COP26. It supports SDG 7 and SDG 13 and gives a voice to the Global South.

questions.q:
A UN World Water Development Report 2026 was released around World Water Day. Consider the following statements:
1. It was based on the 2026 theme 'Water and Gender'.
2. It found that 2.1 billion people still lack safely managed drinking water.
3. It found that men and boys are the main collectors of water in most households.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Women and girls, not men and boys, are the primary water collectors, spending over 250 million hours a day on the task and losing time for education and income, so statement 3 is wrong.

questions.q:
International Day of Forests was observed in March 2026. Consider the following statements:
1. The UN General Assembly proclaimed the day in 2012, and it was first observed in 2013.
2. The 2026 theme was 'Forests and Economies'.
3. It falls on the same date as World Water Day.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: International Day of Forests is on 21 March, a day before World Water Day on 22 March, so statement 3 is wrong. The 2026 theme, 'Forests and Economies', links conservation with livelihoods and development.
questions.h: One day before World Water Day.

questions.q:
On World Water Day (22 March 2026), carrying the UN theme 'Water and Gender', the Ministry of Jal Shakti's conclave released several publications. Consider the following statements:
1. The 7th Minor Irrigation Census was released.
2. The 2nd Census of Springs was released.
3. The National Water Data Policy 2026 was released.
4. The conclave theme was 'Industry for Water'.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: It was the first Census of Springs, along with the 2nd Census of Water Bodies. FICCI, ASSOCHAM and CII committed to water audits by 2027 and Zero Liquid Discharge by 2030.

questions.q:
The Delhi government partnered with IIT Madras to test titanium dioxide (TiO2) photocatalytic coatings on roads and surfaces. Consider the following statements:
1. Under sunlight, the coatings break down nitrogen dioxide and volatile organic compounds.
2. They directly remove primary PM2.5 and PM10 from the air.
3. Concerns include nitrate runoff into water bodies such as the Yamuna.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The coatings act on gaseous pollutants that go on to form secondary particulates and ground-level ozone; they do not remove primary PM2.5 and PM10, so statement 2 is wrong. Nitrate runoff into the Yamuna is one of the concerns.
questions.h: They treat gases, not primary dust.

questions.q:
An ISRO study found that the 2025 Dharali flash flood in Uttarakhand had a specific cause. Consider the following statements:
1. The flood followed the sudden collapse of an exposed ice patch in the Srikanta Glacier's nivation zone.
2. The study concluded that it was a Glacial Lake Outburst Flood.
3. Dharali is in Uttarakhand.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The study ruled out a cloudburst and a GLOF, identifying ice-patch collapse tied to deglaciation. Nivation is erosion beneath and around a snowbank due to alternate freezing and thawing.

questions.q: The Supreme Court formally disposed of the 1985 PIL filed by environmentalist M.C. Mehta. In this case the Court recognised
o: only the rule of strict liability from Rylands v. Fletcher
the principle of absolute liability and applied the doctrine of public trust to natural resources
the polluter pays principle for the first time in the Vellore case
the basic structure doctrine for environmental law
questions.e: M.C. Mehta led to lead-free petrol, coastal management plans and the shifting of stone crushers out of Delhi. The Godavarman case (1995) widened forest land and Vellore (1996) recognised the precautionary and polluter pays principles.

questions.q:
The Centre for Science and Environment released its State of India's Environment 2026 report. Consider the following statements:
1. CSE is a Delhi-based non-profit that has produced annual reports since 1982.
2. Extreme weather events occurred on 99 per cent of days in 2025.
3. Madhya Pradesh was the worst hit State by number of days.
4. About 85 per cent of Indians live within 10 km of a continuous air quality monitor.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Himachal Pradesh (267 days) was worst hit, then Kerala (173) and Madhya Pradesh (162). Only 15 per cent of the population lives within 10 km of a continuous monitor. The 2025 events caused 4,419 deaths.
questions.h: Only 15 per cent near a monitor.
